title: Gibeah
lead: A town of Benjamin a few miles north of Jerusalem, scene of the crime that started Israel's civil war (Judges 19–20) and later the hometown and capital of King Saul.

sections.b: Gibeah means "hill." In Judges 19 a Levite and his concubine are refused shelter there, and the men of the town attack the house; the outrage leads to war against Benjamin (Judges 20). Later Gibeah is Saul's home and royal seat (1 Samuel 10:26; 11:4; 15:34), and its people gave seven of Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites for execution (2 Samuel 21:6). Hosea twice calls Israel back to "the days of Gibeah" as a byword for deep corruption (Hosea 9:9; 10:9). Isaiah pictures its people fleeing the Assyrians (Isaiah 10:29). Most scholars identify it with Tell el-Ful, where small fortresses of the Iron Age were excavated, though some prefer a nearby site. It is easily confused with Geba, a different town nearby.
